summary: Closed the child question's remaining control gap: the cluster scenario now runs twice in one execution, once restarting the node with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and once restarting it with the feature off, everything else identical including the first life running with the feature enabled so a persisted commit index exists in both runs. Local construction feedback shows the mode is the only difference: with the feature on the restarted node reports the stale {A,B,C}, leads the two-voter partition while the other three voters elect their own leader, and applies a write of its own; with the feature off it reports {A,B,C,D,E}, no node leads the two-voter partition, the cluster has exactly one leader, and the restarted node applies nothing. The experiment is filed under the split-brain question as a revision of its last experiment (same investigation) with seven mode-conditioned comparisons declared per mode, covering the restarted node's reported configuration, minority-partition leadership, single-leader count and the restarted node's own applied writes, so the receipt carries the feature-on and feature-off runs side by side. I deliberately avoided asserting cluster-wide applied-write consistency in the control because that metric is only meaningful when both sides committed a write, and said so in the scope. Incomplete: that receipt and its interpretation, the user Restore and term-changing truncation paths for the repair question, and whether a divergent node would organically fall behind often enough for the snapshot repair to occur.
